title: Standardize timeout configuration (connect/read/overall) and map transport timeouts to TimeoutError
author: Ibrahim Khan
description:
Context: As part of the cross-SDK parity audit, Python timeouts were effectively ambiguous (single float propagated inconsistently) and transport timeouts bubbled up as httpx exceptions with different shapes depending on whether the call was streaming or non-streaming. This shows up in support as “streaming hangs then errors” (SUP-9321) and inconsistent caller handling across services.

This PR standardizes timeout configuration across the Python SDK to match the draft client behavior spec: explicit connect/read/overall timeouts, sensible endpoint-aware defaults (streaming vs non-streaming), and consistent error mapping to a single SDK TimeoutError type.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced a single SDK timeout model: `Timeouts(connect, read, overall)` with clear semantics.
- Standardized defaults:
  - Non-streaming requests (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank): connect=10s, read=60s, overall=90s.
  - Streaming requests: connect=10s, read=300s (idle timeout), overall=None (no overall deadline by default; callers can set one).
- Added per-request override support while keeping a single source of truth for merging defaults + overrides.
- Mapped all underlying transport timeouts (httpx.ConnectTimeout/ReadTimeout/PoolTimeout/TimeoutException) to `redwood.errors.TimeoutError` with consistent fields and message formatting.
- Updated docstrings and README snippets to explicitly describe timeout behavior, especially for streaming.
- Added unit tests covering: connect timeout, read timeout, overall timeout, streaming idle timeout, and error shape.

Non-goals:
- No changes to retry policy here (tracked in PR #412 / ENG-2486).
- No server-side/gateway behavior changes.

Implementation notes:
- We treat `overall` as a deadline for the request lifecycle when set. For streaming, default overall=None avoids unintentionally killing long-lived streams; the `read` timeout acts as an idle timeout (no bytes read) to catch dead connections.
- Error mapping preserves the original exception as `__cause__` and includes a safe, non-secret-bearing context string (method, path, whether streaming).

Docs/Changelog:
- Added a “Timeouts” section and updated parameter docs for `RedwoodClient(...)` and `client.chat.completions.create(...)`.
- Changelog: clarified that behavior is more consistent, with the only user-visible change being that timeout errors are now always `redwood.errors.TimeoutError`.

Test plan:
- `pytest -q` locally
- Added regression tests for SUP-9321-style streaming stalls using a mocked server that accepts and then stops sending bytes.

Related:
- ENG-2486 (Python parity workstream)
- ENG-2489 (error taxonomy)
- PR #412 (retry policy + budget)
- Docs work in redwood-docs PR #904
commits: sdk(timeouts): add Timeouts model and merge logic for defaults + per-request overrides
sdk(http): plumb connect/read/overall into httpx client creation and request execution
errors: map all httpx timeout variants to redwood.errors.TimeoutError w/ stable message and cause
tests: add timeout coverage for connect/read/overall + streaming idle timeout behavior
docs: update docstrings + README timeouts section
changelog: document timeout standardization + migration notes
changed_files: redwood/resources/chat/completions.py (streaming vs non-streaming defaults, call-site merge)
conversation:
Monica Patel (review): Can we be explicit in docs about what `read` means for streaming? Folks assume it’s “time to first token” not “idle timeout”.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Good call. I updated README + docstrings to label `read` as “socket idle timeout (no bytes received)” and added an example recommending `overall=120` if they want a hard deadline.

Rafael Mendes (SRE): Default overall=None for streaming makes sense, but please ensure we don’t hang forever on dead TCP connections.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Yep — default read=300s for streaming is an idle timeout, so dead connections should surface. Added `test_streaming_idle_timeout_triggers` to ensure it consistently raises `TimeoutError`.

Sahana Iyer (CI): Tests look good; please avoid relying on wall-clock sleeps where possible.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Refactored the streaming timeout test to use a deterministic mock server that blocks reads without sleeping, and set the idle timeout to 0.2s in-test.

Elliot Price (Docs): Minor nit: README examples should match TS docs (naming). Are we calling it `Timeouts` across SDKs?

Ibrahim Khan (author): For Python we’re landing `Timeouts` (capital T). Noted in ENG-2491 to ensure cross-language docs use consistent wording even if type names differ. Updated README to describe semantics rather than type name.

Monica Patel (final): Approved once changelog includes a migration note about catching `TimeoutError` instead of httpx exceptions.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Added under “Changed” in CHANGELOG: timeout exceptions are now always `redwood.errors.TimeoutError` (httpx exceptions are wrapped as cause).

Monica Patel: LGTM.

Rafael Mendes: LGTM.
release_notes: Python SDK now supports explicit connect/read/overall timeouts with endpoint-aware defaults (streaming vs non-streaming).
All transport timeout conditions now raise `redwood.errors.TimeoutError` with consistent messaging; underlying httpx exception is preserved as the cause.
Docs and examples updated to clarify streaming timeout semantics (idle timeout vs overall deadline).
